note: Screen 11a mini question after each instrument card (post-it '11a warehouse flow'). One per instrument, 3 options, from the instrument pages.

questions.question: What kind of pictures did Pancam take?
options: Detailed 3-D panoramic pictures of the landscape
X-ray pictures of the inside of rocks
Weather maps of the whole planet
questions.explanation: Pancam's two cameras took detailed, multi-wavelength, 3-D panoramic pictures around the rover.

questions.question: What special feature does Mastcam-Z have?
options: A zoom lens to magnify distant targets
questions.explanation: Mastcam-Z is Perseverance's mast camera system with a zoom function.

questions.question: Where was the Microscopic Imager mounted?
options: On the turret at the end of the robotic arm
questions.explanation: It sat on the arm's turret so it could get extremely close to rocks and soil.

questions.question: Which rover carries MAHLI?
questions.explanation: MAHLI (Mars Hand Lens Imager) is on Curiosity's robotic arm.

questions.question: What does Mini-TES measure?
options: Infrared light (heat) given off by minerals
questions.explanation: Mini-TES measured infrared light emitted by minerals and was tuned to look for minerals formed in water.

questions.question: What does CheMin identify?
options: Minerals in powdered rock or soil
questions.explanation: CheMin uses X-rays to identify minerals in powdered samples delivered by Curiosity's arm.

questions.question: What does the Mössbauer spectrometer identify?
questions.explanation: It determines the makeup and amounts of iron-bearing minerals, like hematite.

questions.question: What does APXS determine?
options: The chemical elements that make up rocks and soils
questions.explanation: APXS reveals the elemental chemistry of rocks and soils using X-rays and alpha particles.

questions.question: What does PIXL measure?
options: The chemical makeup of rocks at a very fine scale
questions.explanation: PIXL, on Perseverance, measures rock chemistry at a very fine scale.

questions.question: Why did the rovers use the Rock Abrasion Tool?
options: To cut samples and send them to Earth
To reveal fresh rock surfaces under the dusty outside
questions.explanation: The RAT's grinding teeth exposed fresh mineral surfaces for the other instruments.

questions.question: What did the Magnet Array collect?
questions.explanation: The magnets collected dust so the instruments could study its composition.

questions.question: What does MEDA do on Perseverance?
questions.explanation: MEDA measures weather and monitors dust with sensors on the rover.

questions.question: What were the calibration targets for?
options: Reference points with known properties to fine-tune the instruments
questions.explanation: Objects with known properties (like the sundial) helped scientists fine-tune their observations.

questions.question: What did MOXIE make on Mars?
questions.explanation: MOXIE produced oxygen from the carbon-dioxide-rich Martian atmosphere.
